questions.q: What three things make up a tool definition in the Claude Messages API?
options: A name, a description, and an input_schema describing its arguments
A price, a rate limit, and a timeout value
A model name, a temperature, and a max_tokens value
A URL, an HTTP method, and a header list
questions.explain: That's the whole definition: name (how it's referenced), description (how the model decides when/how to call it), and input_schema (its arguments, in JSON Schema).

questions.q: Does the model itself ever execute a tool?
options: Yes, Claude runs the tool directly on Anthropic's servers for every tool
No — for tools you define, the model only requests a call via a tool_use block; your application code actually executes it
Only if the tool is written in Python
Yes, but only for tools named 'get_weather'
questions.explain: For your own tools, the model requests the call with a tool_use block; your code is responsible for actually running it and sending back a tool_result.

questions.q: What connects a tool_result block to the specific tool_use block it's answering?
options: They must both be sent in the exact same API request
Nothing connects them — the model infers it from context
The matching tool_use_id value on both blocks
The order they appear in the conversation, with no identifier needed
questions.explain: The tool_result's tool_use_id must match the id Claude generated on the tool_use block, which matters once an agent can make several calls in one turn.

questions.q: What does input_schema use to describe a tool's expected arguments?
options: A plain English paragraph with no structure
Standard JSON Schema — type, properties, and required
A YAML configuration file
A separate XML document
questions.explain: input_schema is standard JSON Schema: type (usually "object"), properties (each argument's type and description), and required (which are mandatory).

questions.q: What does a stop_reason of tool_use tell your application code?
options: The request failed and should be retried from scratch
The conversation has permanently ended
Claude wants a tool run and its result sent back before it can continue
The user needs to approve the request manually before anything happens
questions.explain: stop_reason: tool_use signals the model is waiting on a tool_result; stop_reason: end_turn signals it has already finished with a final answer.
